title: Hilltop Hoods to Headline Castaway Festival Across Three Australian Cities
summary: The Adelaide hip-hop trio tops a lineup with Violent Soho and Amy Shark across three Australian cities this November through March.
body: Hilltop Hoods will headline Australia’s Castaway Festival across three cities this summer, extending a run for the Adelaide hip-hop trio that has made them the most decorated act in the history of the ARIA Albums Chart. The group holds a record seven No. 1 albums on the chart — more than any other Australian act, surpassing AC/DC, Powderfinger, Cold Chisel and Silverchair — a streak that most recently extended with 2025’s Fall From the Light . Castaway will run at Whitfords Nodes Park in Hillarys, Western Australia, on Saturday, Nov. 21; Mornington Racecourse in Victoria on Saturday, Dec. 12; and Wollongong, New South Wales, on Saturday, March 20, 2027. Joining Hilltop Hoods on the bill are Brisbane rock band Violent Soho and ARIA-winning singer-songwriter Amy Shark, alongside supporting acts Playlunch, Trials, Lyric and Birdland. General tickets go on sale Friday, Aug. 28, with artist, promoter and Telstra Plus presales opening Wednesday, Aug. 26. Hilltop Hoods have built one of the most substantial catalogs in Australian hip-hop over more than two decades. title: إنفانتينو يعلن إقامة كأس العالم تحت 15 سنة بمشاركة 211 منتخبا

title: Australian Promoter Fuzzy Rebrands for 30th Anniversary
summary: “Thirty years is a huge milestone in live music, particularly when you think about how much the industry has changed since 1996,” said Fuzzy CEO Adelle Robinson.
body: Australian live music promoter Fuzzy has launched a new brand identity to mark its 30th anniversary, unifying its portfolio of festivals and touring business under the Fuzzy name for the first time. The company, now led by CEO Adelle Robinson , traces its roots to 1996, when co-founders John Wall and Ming Gan launched Sublime, an 800-capacity club night on Sydney’s Pitt Street. By 2000, that had grown into Parklife, a national touring festival that helped popularize Australia’s “indie-dance” movement before folding into Listen Out in 2013. Fuzzy went on to build a portfolio that includes Field Day, Harbourlife and Shore Thing, and has credited itself with helping break acts including Flume, who played a small Parklife stage as a Triple J Unearthed winner in 2012 before returning to headline Listen Out and Field Day within a decade. Wall and Gan stepped away from the company in 2025; Ming Gan retired that December, with Robinson — Fuzzy’s managing director since its early years — stepping into the CEO role. summary: The band will perform 1996 breakthrough Bringing Down the Horse in full for its 30th anniversary.
body: The Wallflowers will play Australia for the first time, announcing a five-date tour presented by Love Police to mark the 30th anniversary of their breakthrough album, Bringing Down the Horse . The band will perform the album in full at every show. The tour opens at Melbourne’s Palais Theatre on Friday, Dec. 4, followed by Thirroul’s Anita’s Theatre on Dec. 5, Sydney’s Liberty Hall on Dec. 6, Brisbane’s Fortitude Music Hall on Dec. 8 and Adelaide’s Hindley Street Music Hall on Dec. 9. A promoter presale begins Wednesday, Aug. 26, with general tickets on sale Friday, Aug. 28. Bringing Down the Horse , released May 21, 1996, peaked at No. 4 on the Billboard 200 and was certified quadruple platinum in the U.S.; in Australia it went gold and reached No. 9 on the ARIA chart. Lead single “One Headlight” became the band’s signature hit, topping Billboard’s Mainstream Rock, Modern Rock and Triple-A airplay charts simultaneously and winning two Grammy Awards in 1998 for best rock song and best rock performance by a duo or group with vocals. title: Another major Android phone maker caves to soaring RAM costs with price hikes
summary: Xiaomi says it can no longer manintain competitive prices for some of its models thanks to the memory crunch.
body: TL;DR Xiaomi is raising prices on several smartphones and tablets by up to ¥20,000 (~$137), citing soaring memory and component costs. The Xiaomi 17T Pro and several POCO X8 Pro models will get the biggest increases, with some models becoming around 25% more expensive. Xiaomi’s latest move is another sign that the memory shortage is forcing smartphone makers to pass higher component costs on to consumers. The RAM crisis is starting to hit smartphone prices hard, and Xiaomi is the latest major Android phone maker to cave to rising component costs. The company has announced price increases for several smartphones and tablets, with some devices getting a hefty ¥20,000 (~$137) increase. Xiaomi says soaring memory prices and other rising product costs have become too difficult for the company to absorb.

body: ماذا قال؟ اختار المصري حمزة عبد الكريم أن يرد على عدم مشاركته في مواجهة برشلونة أمام إلتشي برسالة هادئة تحمل قدرًا كبيرًا من الثقة والصبر، مؤكدًا أن الفرصة قد لا تأتي اليوم، لكن الأهم بالنسبة له هو الاستعداد الكامل للحظة التي يحين فيها موعد الظهور. وكتب مهاجم برشلونة الشاب عبر حساباته على مواقع التواصل الاجتماعي عقب المباراة: "لا دقائق اليوم. يبقى التركيز قائمًا. سأظل مستعدًا لحظة المشاركة عندما تأتي"، في رسالة عكست تعامله الإيجابي مع قرار عدم الدفع به، وتمسكه بالاستعداد بدلًا من الانشغال بغيابه عن أرض الملعب. وجاءت رسالة حمزة عقب الانتصار الكبير الذي حققه برشلونة على إلتشي بنتيجة 5-0، في مباراة اعتمد خلالها الألماني هانزي فليك على رافينيا في مركز المهاجم الصريح، بينما منح الدقائق الهجومية لأسماء أخرى، في ظل المنافسة القوية على مراكز الخط الأمامي. ورغم عدم حصوله على فرصة المشاركة، بدا حمزة حريصًا على إرسال رسالة مختلفة تمامًا؛ إذ لم يتضمن حديثه أي اعتراض أو شكوى، وإنما ركز على الجاهزية وانتظار الفرصة، وهي العقلية التي يحتاجها اللاعب الشاب في بداية تجربته مع الفريق الأول.

body: The Kindle Oasis was released in 2019, and it’s been a while since Amazon added a meaningful update to the system. So, when I learned that Amazon was rolling out a new system software update this past week, I was quite excited. That’s until I learned that the update closes a long-standing loophole for library books borrowed via Libby that lets you hold onto a book longer than you’d otherwise be allowed. Additionally, it further tightens DRM to ensure buyers can’t offload books from the Kindle. While the first feature doesn’t affect me much, the latter, as someone who likes preserving digital media, makes the update an instant no-go for me. On paper, these changes protect publishers’ rights and intellectual property. For the end user, though, they are just another reminder that you never truly own your digital library or even the hardware you technically bought.
